title: Chicken With Balsamic on a Sheet Pan
description: From “Everyday Dorie” Greenspan: “This dish has already become a favorite among so many home cooks – and I understand why. The recipe’s a quickie – quick to put together and not too long to cook. The “main course” is chicken legs (although you can use breasts; see below) and the “sides” are roasted baby potatoes and mushrooms with shallots and garlic. The flavorings are simple: oil, balsamic vinegar (a brand just a step up from the most basic makes a better dish) and fresh herbs. And what comes out of the oven is seductive. It’s the perfect recipe for a during-the-week meal after a crazy-busy day, although it’s just as good on the weekends, when you’ve got more time but might want to spend it away from the kitchen. If you’ve got a crowd coming, double the recipe and use two pans.”
ingredients: 11⁄2 pounds (680 grams) small potatoes, scrubbed and halved if large
1⁄2 pound (226 grams) white mushrooms, wiped clean, trimmed and cut in half if large
1 or 2 large shallots or medium onions, cut into 8 wedges, rinsed and patted dry
Fine sea salt and freshly ground pepper
4 whole chicken legs (thighs and drumsticks, or just 8 thighs), patted dry
directions: Center a rack in the oven and preheat it to 450 degrees F. Rub a baking sheet with a little oil (or line it with foil and oil the foil).

Put the potatoes, mushrooms, shallot or onion and garlic in a large bowl. Toss in 4 sprigs each of the rosemary and thyme, 1 teaspoon salt, a few grindings of pepper, 3 tablespoons of the oil and a big dash or two of the balsamic. Mix everything well and spread the ingredients out on the baking sheet.
Put the chicken in the bowl, along with the remaining 3 tablespoons oil and 2 tablespoons balsamic,
1⁄2 teaspoon salt and a good amount of pepper, and mix well to coat the chicken. Move the vegetables around to make room for the chicken. Tuck the remaining herbs under each piece.
Roast the chicken for 30 minutes or so, until a thermometer stuck into the thickest part of a thigh measures 165 degrees F.
Serve everything on the baking sheet or a big platter; pour the cooking juices over the chicken.
